newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-ALLEN EXERCISES OPTION TO BUY SEAHAWKS, KEEP IN SEATTLE.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-ALLEN EXERCISES OPTION TO BUY SEAHAWKS, KEEP IN SEATTLE.

text.p: Billionaire Paul Allen exercised his option to buy the National Football League's Seattle Seahawks Monday, fulfilling a promise to Washington state voters who approved the Microsoft Corp co-founder's proposed $425 million football stadium.
Officials of Allen's Football Northwest Inc did not disclose the price he is paying but media reports have put it at about $200 million.
Allen bought the option in April 1996 after being approached by local political and business leaders who wanted to block current owner Ken Behring's attempt to move the team to California.
The option would have expired July 1, and Allen had said he would walk away from the deal unless the state's voters ratified a plan to use public money to build a new stadium in downtown Seattle.

By a 51-49 percent margin, voters approved the $325 million tax package June 17, paving the way for a new open-air stadium to replace the 21-year-old Kingdome, possibly in time for the 2002 NFL season. The remainder of the stadium's cost is being guaranteed by Allen.
The stadium project will join a $414 million retractable-roof baseball stadium being built adjacent to the Kingdome.

Allen, who ranks as the third-wealthiest U.S. individual with a $13 billion Microsoft stake, also said in a statement that the team was putting on sale 7,000 tickets per game at $10 each, the lowest price in the NFL.
